section_summary: This section chiefly documents narcotics smuggling, opium addiction, and the government opium monopoly in Dairen and the Kwantung Leased Territory from 1935 through 1939. It includes lists of suspected traffickers, consular assessments of the illicit trade, detailed translations of Japanese opium-control ordinances, statistics on licensed addicts, and criticism of the monopoly’s substantial revenue and limited success in reducing addiction. The final pages contain 1930 regulations governing opium transportation aboard Japanese ships and correspondence about sensational newspaper claims that enormous quantities of cocaine were being advertised for sale in Japan.

subfiles.title: Conclusion of report on narcotics manufacture in Chinese localities
subfiles.about: Reports that military and local figures became involved in narcotics manufacture at several Chinese localities.
subfiles.summary: Concluding fragment names Generals Yui Kue-Chai, Cho Ming-Chi and Wang Feng-Min as linked to narcotics manufacture; Nicholson's agent will report more.

subfiles.title: Transmittal of Treasury Attaché Nicholson’s Dairen suspect list
subfiles.about: Transmits two copies of Nicholson’s September 23 report identifying suspected narcotics smugglers present in Dairen.
subfiles.summary: Treasury forwards Nicholson's confidential report naming suspected smugglers in Dairen on September 15, 1935.

subfiles.title: Dairen Agent Report: smugglers and suspects
subfiles.from: M. R. Nicholson, Treasury attaché, Shanghai
subfiles.about: Lists the names and Dairen addresses of numerous suspected smugglers and narcotics associates.
subfiles.summary: Agent report lists suspects in Dairen on September 15, 1935 with addresses, including Igolkowsky, Shpraus and Kobzareff of the North-Manchuria Transport Company and associates; more lists promised.

subfiles.title: Effects of Recent Chinese Legislation on Drug Traffic
subfiles.from: Troy L. Perkins, American vice consul, Dairen
subfiles.about: Assesses the limited direct effect of Chinese drug laws on Japanese-administered Kwantung and summarizes opium revenue, imports, illicit trafficking, and addiction treatment.
subfiles.summary: Perkins: recent Chinese legislation barely applies in Kwantung; large 1934 opium imports via Dairen; extensive illicit manufacture and transshipment; the Dairen addict home treated about 5,000 in ten years, with three to four percent of residents needing treatment.

subfiles.title: Cross-reference to Nanking despatch on Kwantung narcotics control
subfiles.about: Directs researchers to another file containing a despatch on narcotics control in the Kwantung Leased Territory.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference: Nanking despatch of September 12, 1935 on narcotics control in the Kwantung Leased Territory (894C.01/84).

subfiles.title: Confidential transmittal of report on the Kwantung Leased Territory
subfiles.about: Sends a confidential copy of an August 19 report on Kwantung for the Commissioner of Narcotics.
subfiles.summary: State forwards a report on Kwantung, an unusual administrative area and illicit narcotics source, directing attention to its budget and narcotics control.

subfiles.title: Cross-reference to Treasury letter transmitting Nicholson reports
subfiles.about: Cross-references a Treasury Department letter transmitting copies of reports by Treasury Attaché Nicholson.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference: November 6, 1935 Treasury letter transmitting Nicholson's Shanghai reports (893.114 Narcotics/1340).

subfiles.title: Transmittal of Dairen despatch on Chinese narcotics legislation
subfiles.about: Forwards Dairen despatch No. 76 on the effect of recent Chinese legislation on narcotics traffic in Kwantung.
subfiles.summary: Department sends the Narcotics Commissioner two confidential copies of the October 3, 1935 Dairen despatch on Chinese drug legislation in Kwantung.

subfiles.title: Cross-reference concerning Harold S. Jones’s death
subfiles.about: Points to information concerning Harold S. Jones’s death at Dairen from morphine poisoning.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference: November 8, 1935 letter on Harold S. Jones's fatal morphine poisoning (311.113 Jones.Harold S./2).

subfiles.title: Transmittal of material concerning Curt Smith and Max Kattwinkel
subfiles.from: Wayne C. Taylor, Assistant Secretary of the Treasury
subfiles.about: Forwards a Paris Treasury attaché’s letter and enclosures about Curt Smith and Kattwinkel’s statement to German narcotics authorities.
subfiles.summary: Treasury sends the acting attaché's September 19 letter and Kattwinkel's August 28 statement to the German Central Narcotics Office on Curt Smith's suspected narcotics involvement.

subfiles.title: Acting Treasury attaché’s transmittal of the Curt Smith memorandum
subfiles.from: J. Homer Butler, Acting Treasury Attaché, Paris
subfiles.about: Transmits Charles B. Dyar’s memorandum and a translation of Kattwinkel’s statement about Curt Smith.
subfiles.summary: Butler forwards Dyar's September 14 memorandum on Smith and Kattwinkel's translated statement, with copies to Nicholson.

subfiles.title: Memorandum concerning Curt Smith and Kattwinkel
subfiles.from: Charles B. Dyar, Special Agent, Bureau of Narcotics
subfiles.about: Forwards Kattwinkel’s statement and discusses evidence that Smith’s transactions may have been commercial swindles.
subfiles.summary: Dyar: the German Central Narcotics Office thinks Smith's transactions may be swindles; British authorities asked for evidence from injured merchants; mentions Berlin merchant Willy Stieler.

subfiles.title: Statement of Max Friedrich Kattwinkel
subfiles.about: Describes Kattwinkel’s dealings with Curt Smith, alleges misuse of his firm and credit in fraudulent shipments, and denies any personal involvement in narcotics.
subfiles.summary: Max Kattwinkel says Smith used his power of attorney to draw about £12,000 against worthless or overvalued goods shipped to Hong Kong and Dairen; calls them invoice swindles, denies any narcotics role, and offers help to German authorities.

subfiles.title: Thompson warning on the Dairen narcotics-smuggling network
subfiles.from: Berger, transmitting a message from Beriah M. Thompson
subfiles.to: Secretary of State for the Secretary of the Treasury
subfiles.about: Warns of a large European-operated narcotics-smuggling network based in Dairen and names shippers and routes requiring surveillance.
subfiles.summary: Thompson warns of a large Dairen narcotics racket run by Europeans in shipping, urging inspection of vessels and cargoes from Dairen, especially soybean oil, and ships at Newchwang and Hulutao.

subfiles.title: Transmittal of Thompson’s narcotics-smuggling telegram
subfiles.about: Forwards the Tientsin telegram containing Thompson’s report on illicit narcotics traffic in Korea, Manchuria, and Kwantung.
subfiles.summary: State encloses two copies of the November 2 Tientsin telegram relaying retired Commander Beriah Thompson's report to the Treasury Secretary.

subfiles.title: Cross-reference to Japan’s 1935 annual narcotics report
subfiles.about: Cross-references Japan’s annual report for 1935 under League of Nations document number C.541.M.350.1936.XI.
subfiles.summary: The file note points to file 894.114 Narcotics/252. It identifies the referenced item as Japan’s annual report for 1935.

subfiles.title: Cross-reference to report on A. Beerbrayer
subfiles.about: Cross-references a report from China concerning suspected trafficker A. Beerbrayer.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference: Treasury letter transmitting a report from China on A. Beerbrayer's activities (811.111 Beerbrayer.A.).

subfiles.title: Developments in the Opium Monopoly of the Kwantung Leased Territory
subfiles.from: William T. Turner, American consul, Dairen
subfiles.about: Explains new Kwantung opium laws, the conversion of the monopoly into a manufacturing enterprise, and doubts about whether tighter controls will reduce addiction.
subfiles.summary: Turner reports that Imperial Ordinance No. 84 and Kwantung Bureau Ordinance No. 8 centralize the manufacture of prepared opium in the Kwantung Monopoly Bureau and tighten controls on dealers, permits, and addicts. Director Noboru Yasunaga argues that the new Port Arthur factory and stricter rules will eliminate abuses and ultimately reduce addiction. Turner acknowledges that the machinery permits better control but questions whether the government will sacrifice lucrative opium revenue, noting experience in Korea and Taiwan, attractive monopoly packaging, generous retailer profits, and the open availability of bootleg opium. He proposes later reports on the factory and government sanitarium.

subfiles.title: Imperial Ordinance No. 84 and Kwantung Bureau Ordinance No. 7
subfiles.from: Japanese government; translated by William T. Turner
subfiles.about: Amends the Kwantung opium law to establish official manufacture and stricter possession rules and orders the amendments into force.
subfiles.summary: Imperial Ordinance 84 gives authorities the sale and manufacture of prepared and medicinal opium, bars retailers from adulterating it, and sets penalties; Bureau Ordinance 7 enforces it from February 21, 1938.

subfiles.title: Kwantung Bureau Ordinance No. 8: Rules for Enforcement of the Opium Law
subfiles.from: Kwantung Bureau; translated by William T. Turner
subfiles.to: Kwantung authorities, opium dealers, medical professionals, and permitted smokers
subfiles.about: Sets comprehensive rules for licensing smokers, distributing opium, regulating dealers, maintaining records, reporting transactions, and punishing violations.
subfiles.summary: The ordinance requires adult Manchurian or Chinese addicts to obtain certificates specifying their dosage and designated dealer, generally limiting possession to ten days’ supply. It makes the Kwantung Monopoly Bureau responsible for distributing opium and manufacturing prepared and medicinal opium, while regulating medical, experimental, and retail access. Dealers must buy from the monopoly, sell only to designated permit holders, keep detailed records, and report monthly to police. The final articles establish business sanctions, imprisonment, fines, and derivative responsibility for employees, representatives, and juridical persons.

subfiles.title: Opium Addiction in the Kwantung Leased Territory
subfiles.from: William T. Turner, American consul, Dairen
subfiles.about: Reports the Kwantung government’s official count of permitted opium smokers.
subfiles.summary: Turner supplements his March 24 report: 28,197 addicts held police smoking permits in the Kwantung territory as of April 6.

subfiles.title: Transmittal of Kwantung opium-control ordinances and package photographs
subfiles.about: Forwards Turner’s monopoly report, translated ordinances, and photostats of an opium tube and carton to the Commissioner of Narcotics.
subfiles.summary: Department sends Dairen Despatch 9 with translations of Ordinances 84 and 8, highlighting penalties for retailers who adulterate opium, and has requested Ordinances 389 of 1934 and 7 of 1937.

subfiles.title: Acknowledgment and request for earlier Kwantung opium ordinances
subfiles.from: R. Walton Moore for the Secretary of State
subfiles.to: William T. Turner, American consul, Dairen
subfiles.about: Commends Turner’s report and requests copies and translations of the 1934 and 1937 amendments.
subfiles.summary: Department rates Turner's March 24 report Very Good, plans to send it to the Opium Advisory Committee representative, and requests five copies of Ordinances 389 of 1934 and 7 of 1937.

subfiles.title: Transmitting Opium Control Law
subfiles.from: William T. Turner, American consul, Dairen
subfiles.about: Supplies translations of the requested 1934 and 1937 amendments to the Kwantung Opium Ordinance.
subfiles.summary: Turner forwards translations of Imperial Ordinance 389 of December 26, 1934 and Ordinance 7 of February 1, 1937.

subfiles.title: Imperial Ordinance No. 389 of December 26, 1934
subfiles.from: Japanese government; translated by William T. Turner
subfiles.about: Transfers powers under the Kwantung Opium Ordinance from the governor to the Japanese ambassador to Manchukuo.
subfiles.summary: Ordinance 389 replaces references to the Governor of Kwantung with the Ambassador Plenipotentiary to Manchukuo.

subfiles.title: Imperial Ordinance No. 7 of February 1, 1937
subfiles.from: Japanese government; translated by William T. Turner
subfiles.about: Creates severe penalties for causing or assisting minors to smoke, possess, or transfer opium.
subfiles.summary: Ordinance 7 sets up to seven years' penal servitude or a ¥5,000 fine for involving persons under twenty-one in opium smoking or possession, with lesser penalties for abetting; effective February 21, 1937.

subfiles.title: Transmittal of 1934 and 1937 Kwantung opium ordinances
subfiles.about: Forwards Turner’s June 6 despatch and translations of Imperial Ordinances Nos. 389 and 7 to the Commissioner of Narcotics.
subfiles.summary: Department supplies duplicate copies of the Dairen despatch and two translated ordinances on narcotics control in Kwantung.

subfiles.title: Kwantung Opium Monopoly
subfiles.from: William T. Turner, American consul, Dairen
subfiles.about: Transmits a newspaper report showing continued addiction and argues that monopoly profits discourage decisive suppression.
subfiles.summary: Turner concludes stricter 1938 laws have not reduced addiction, which may have risen among Japanese in Dairen; he bought non-monopoly opium openly at a hotel and restaurant; monopoly revenue of about ¥2.2 million was a large part of a ¥23 million budget.

subfiles.title: Newspaper report on addiction and the Kwantung Sanitarium
subfiles.about: Reports increasing opium addiction, more than 1,000 registered Japanese addicts in Dairen, and plans for compulsory treatment.
subfiles.summary: Article: compulsory cures and enforcement have failed, with more addicts dead in cold weather; Dairen has over 1,000 Japanese addicts; a blacklist and intensified treatment planned; sanitarium chief Sakui says unemployed patients relapse.

subfiles.title: Transmittal of despatch on Kwantung addiction and opium revenue
subfiles.about: Forwards Turner’s November 29 despatch and newspaper enclosure concerning addiction levels and monopoly profit.
subfiles.summary: Department sends Treasury duplicates of Despatch 60 on Kwantung addiction and opium revenue, with a copy for the Public Health Service.

subfiles.title: Cross-reference to Kwantung opium-trade statistics
subfiles.about: Points to a despatch presenting statistics from Statistics of Trade in the Kwantung Territory, 1937.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference: May 8, 1939 Dairen despatch on opium-trade statistics from a Kwantung Bureau publication (893.11416 Manchuria/341).

subfiles.title: Despatch transmitting Japanese shipboard opium-transport regulations
subfiles.from: W. R. Castle, Jr., American ambassador, Tokyo
subfiles.about: Transmits a translation of Japanese Communications Department Ordinance No. 5 governing opium transportation aboard Japanese ships.
subfiles.summary: Castle forwards the March 17, 1930 Official Gazette regulation on when Japanese vessels may lawfully carry opium and reporting duties.

subfiles.title: Ordinance No. 5: Rules Relating to Transportation of Opium on Ships
subfiles.from: Matajiro Koizumi, Japanese minister of communications
subfiles.about: Regulates authorized opium carriage by Japanese ships, requires detailed reports for foreign transport, and sets penalties for violations.
subfiles.summary: Ordinance 5: Japanese ships may carry opium only between authorized Japanese territories, in lawful international trade, or complying with foreign domestic laws; captains must report cargo details through consulates; penalties extend to representatives, supervisors and charterers.

subfiles.title: Transmittal of Japanese opium-shipping ordinance to Treasury
subfiles.about: Forwards the Tokyo embassy despatch and translation of Ordinance No. 5 for Treasury information.
subfiles.summary: State sends Treasury Despatch 72 with the Japanese opium-shipping regulation published in the March 17 Official Gazette.

subfiles.title: Transmittal of Japanese opium-shipping ordinance to Commerce
subfiles.about: Forwards the Tokyo embassy despatch and translation of Ordinance No. 5 for Commerce Department information.
subfiles.summary: State sends Commerce Despatch 72 and the translated regulation on opium transport aboard Japanese vessels.

subfiles.title: Inquiry concerning cocaine advertisements reported in the Washington Herald
subfiles.about: Requests the name and date of the Japanese trade paper allegedly advertising hundreds of tons of cocaine for sale in Tokyo.
subfiles.summary: Caldwell quotes Kenneth Clark's April 29 Washington Herald article reproducing ads offering 100 and 1,000 tons of cocaine in Tokyo, asks whether Treasury was the source and for the trade paper's title and date.

subfiles.title: Sales of Dope Advertised by Paper in Japan
subfiles.about: Claims that a Japanese trade paper advertised enormous quantities of cocaine and describes worldwide illicit-drug routes.
subfiles.summary: Article reproduces purported advertisements offering up to 1,000 or 1,800 tons of cocaine in Tokyo, alleging trafficking through Shanghai and Xiamen to India, the Straits, Canada and the US, and supply from French and Swiss factories.
